engineering.basic.name: Engineering / Technical report

title_page.guidance:
The cover page is automatically generated with the project data.
You don't need to write content here.

table_of_contents.guidance:
The index is generated automatically.
You don't need to write anything here.

abstract_es.title: Summary
abstract_es.guidance:
Technical summary of 150–250 words. In engineering it must be specific:
• Problem that the work solves.
• Approach or technology used.
• Main result (metric, performance, improvement).
• Conclusion or key contribution.
No references, no equations, no undefined acronyms.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.guidance:
Contextualize the technical problem and motivate the work:
• Context: technological area, industry or application.
• Motivation: why is it important to solve this problem?
• Related works: very brief review of existing solutions and their limitations.
• Objective and specific contribution of the work.
• Document organization.
In IEEE, citations are numerical: [1], [2], [3].

problem_statement.title: Problem Statement
problem_statement.guidance:
Define the technical problem with formal precision:
• Detailed description of the problem: symptoms, context, restrictions.
• Functional and non-functional requirements.
• Success Criteria: How will you know you solved it?
• Scope and limitations of the project.
• Minimum necessary theoretical framework: concepts, models or theories on which the solution is based.
Use diagrams, requirements tables and use cases if applicable.

design.title: Design and architecture
design.guidance:
Present the proposed solution before implementing it:
• System architecture (component diagram, layers, modules).
• Design decisions and justification of chosen technologies.
• Flowchart or main algorithm.
• Data model if applicable (ER, DB schema).
• User interface (wireframes or mockups if applicable).
The design should be independent of the implementation — a third party should be able to implement it from this section.

implementation.title: Implementation
implementation.guidance:
Describe how the solution was built:
• Development environment: languages, frameworks, platforms, versions.
• Description of the modules or components implemented.
• Relevant code fragments (only the most illustrative ones, not the entire code).
• Implementation challenges and solutions adopted.
• Infrastructure configuration if applicable (servers, containers, DB).
The complete code goes in Annexes — here only the most representative.

testing.title: Testing and validation
testing.guidance:
Demonstrate that the solution works and meets the requirements:
• Test plan: types (unitary, integration, system, acceptance).
• Test cases: input, action, expected result, obtained result.
• Performance metrics if applicable (response time, memory usage, precision).
• Comparison with baseline or related work.
• Analysis of results: what worked? no? because?
Present results in tables or graphs when possible.

conclusions.title: Conclusions and future work
conclusions.guidance:
Close the work with technical rigor:
• Review of the objectives achieved vs. those raised.
• Original contributions of the work.
• Identified technical limitations.
• Future work: concrete improvements, possible extensions, open problems.
In IEEE it is common to mention possible publications or industrial applications.

references.title: References
references.guidance:
In IEEE the references are numerical and appear in order of first mention.
The list is automatically generated from your .bib when you compile.
For IEEE articles and conferences: use the DOI importer to get the correct entry.
Be sure to include the DOI in each reference — IEEE requires it.

appendices.title: Annexes
appendices.guidance:
Complementary technical material:
• Complete source code (main modules).
• Installation and configuration scripts.
• User or technical manuals.
• Detailed diagrams (full ERD, sequence diagrams, etc.).
• Test data or datasets.
Number: Appendix A, B… and refer to them from the main text.

engineering.basic.description: Technical report with sections on approach, design, implementation and testing. IEEE Bibliography. Ideal for engineering thesis and professional residency.

generic.phd.name: Graduate thesis

title_page.guidance:
The cover page is automatically generated with the project data.
For postgraduate studies, configure in the metadata: full name, director, co-director (if applicable) and synodal committee.
You don't need to write content here.

table_of_contents.guidance:
The table of contents is generated automatically.
You don't need to write anything here.

list_of_figures.guidance:
The list of figures is automatically generated from all titled figures in your thesis.
Activate this section if you have 5 or more figures.

list_of_tables.guidance:
The list of tables is automatically generated from all tables with title.
Activate this section if you have 5 or more tables.

list_of_algorithms.guidance:
Automatically generated list of algorithms for computational or engineering theses.
Only activate if you present 3 or more pseudocodes or numbered algorithms.

acronyms.title: List of Abbreviations and Acronyms
acronyms.guidance:
List all acronyms and abbreviations used in the thesis with their full meaning.
Format: ACRONYM — Full meaning (e.g. CNN — Convolutional Neural Network).
Sort alphabetically. It also defines the first time each acronym appears in the text.

abstract_es.title: Summary
abstract_es.guidance:
The graduate summary answers in 250–350 words:
• Motivation: why is this problem important?
• Problem: What question or hypothesis are you addressing?
• Method: main approach and technique.
• Contribution: results and original contribution to the state of the art.
• Impact: theoretical or practical implications.
No citations. No equations. 5–8 Keywords at the end.

abstract_en.title: Abstract
abstract_en.guidance:
Accurate translation of the summary into English. Not a machine translation — check it.
Keywords: in English, preferably terms from the thesaurus of your discipline.
Mandatory for postgraduate studies — it is the version that appears in international repositories.

dedication.title: Dedication
dedication.guidance:
Short and personal text. Dedicate work to those who deserve it most.
No special formatting — the profile is centered on a separate page.

acknowledgements.title: Thanks
acknowledgements.guidance:
Formally thank those who contributed to the work:
• Thesis director and co-director.
• Synodal committee / reviewers.
• Funders: scholarships, projects, institutions (mandatory for projects with external support).
• Technical collaborators, laboratories, companies.
• Family and personal support (at the end, briefly).
Length: half a page.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.guidance:
The introduction of a postgraduate thesis is more demanding than that of a bachelor's degree. You must:
1. Contextualize the problem in the current state of the art.
2. Identify the specific knowledge gap that your thesis addresses.
3. Clearly state the hypothesis or research question.
4. List the objectives (general and specific).
5. Describe the original contribution (what is new in your work?).
6. Justify the scope and delimitations.
7. Describe the organization of the chapters.
A doctoral committee will evaluate whether the contribution is original and independent. Be precise.
Typical length: 5–10 pages.

literature_review.title: Review of Literature and State of the Art
literature_review.guidance:
This is the section that demonstrates your mastery of the field. You must:
• Systematically cover relevant works from the last 5–10 years (classics may be older).
• Organize by theme, focus, or chronology — not as a list of summaries.
• Critically compare the proposals: strengths, weaknesses, limitations.
• Identify the gap that your thesis fills ("no previous work has addressed X").
• End with a comparative table of related works if possible.
For doctorate: this review must be exhaustive and cover all aspects of the problem.
Strategy: Search Scopus, WoS, ACM DL, IEEE Xplore. Use the DOI importer for each article.

theoretical_framework.title: Theoretical Framework
theoretical_framework.guidance:
Develop the theoretical and mathematical foundations necessary to understand your proposal.
Unlike the literature review, here you delve into the key concepts:
• Formal definitions and mathematical notation.
• Theoretical models on which your work is based.
• Relevant theorems or properties (with citations or proof if original).
Activate this section if your thesis requires more than 5–6 pages of theoretical basis.

problem_statement.title: Problem Statement and Hypotheses
problem_statement.guidance:
Formally define the problem that your thesis solves:
• Precise formulation: in exact sciences, use mathematical notation if applicable.
• Hypotheses or research conjectures (for doctorate: verifiable and falsifiable hypothesis).
• Assumptions and restrictions of the model.
• Why the problem is difficult: computational complexity, lack of data, theoretical ambiguity.
• Evaluation criteria: how will you measure the success of your proposal?
This section should be able to be read independently as a problem specification.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.guidance:
Describes the methodological approach with the rigor required by the postgraduate level:
• Research paradigm: positivist, constructivist, mixed.
• Type of research: experimental, quasi-experimental, case study, simulation, modeling.
• Specific research design.
• Data sources: origin, characteristics, collection or generation process.
• Pipeline or complete process from data to results.
• Specific tools, languages, libraries and versions.
Enough detail for complete replicability.

experimentation.title: Experimentation and Development
experimentation.guidance:
Document the development or experimentation process in detail:
• Experimental setup: hardware, hyperparameters, test conditions.
• Experiments performed and their purpose (ablation study, comparison of variants).
• Relevant intermediate observations (not just the final result).
• Decisions made during the process and their justification.
Activate this section if your work has a significant experimental component
separable from the general methodology.

results.title: Results
results.guidance:
Present the results with the statistical rigor required by the postgraduate course:
• Organize by objective or hypothesis.
• For quantitative results: mean, standard deviation, confidence intervals, statistical significance.
• Comparative tables with baseline, own variants and state of the art.
• Figures with error bars when applicable.
• For qualitative results: theoretical saturation, triangulation, representative quotes.
Don't interpret here — just present the data.

discussion.title: Discussion
discussion.guidance:
The discussion of a postgraduate thesis must demonstrate scientific maturity:
• Interpret each result in relation to your hypothesis.
• Compare with state-of-the-art works: do you surpass, equal, or fall short?
• Explains discrepancies with theoretical foundations.
• Discuss theoretical implications: what does it mean for the field?
• Discuss practical implications: what applications are derived?
• Honest limitations: Don't hide weaknesses, the committee will see them anyway.
• Threats to validity if applicable (internal, external, construct validity).

conclusions.title: Conclusions and Future Work
conclusions.guidance:
Close the thesis with a researcher's vision:
• Responds directly to each specific objective set.
• Clearly states the original contribution to knowledge.
• For doctorate: demonstrates that the contribution meets the criteria of originality and independence.
• Specific and realistic future work: open problems, extensions, applications.
• Final reflection on the impact of work on the discipline.
Typical length: 3–5 pages.

references.title: References
references.guidance:
The reference list is automatically generated from your .bib when compiling with APA 7.
For postgraduate studies, 80–200+ high-quality references (indexed articles, technical books) are expected.
Use the DOI importer to add articles from Crossref with one click.
Avoid references to blogs, Wikipedia, or non-peer-reviewed sites as primary sources.

publications.title: Derived Publications
publications.guidance:
List the published or submitted works derived from this thesis:
• Articles in indexed journals (Q1, Q2, Scopus, WoS).
• Presentations at national and international conferences.
• Book chapters, patents, technical reports.
For each: complete reference + status (published / accepted / submitted / in preparation).
Previous publications are a sign of quality and can lighten the defense.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.guidance:
Define specialized terms that a reader who is not an expert in your subspecialty would need to know.
Format: Term — Concise definition.
Do not include terms that have already been defined in the Theoretical Framework — the glossary is for recurring but not central terms.

appendices.title: Annexes
appendices.guidance:
Supplementary technical material that does not belong to the main flow:
• Long or secondary mathematical proofs.
• Source code (main modules, experiment scripts).
• Complete data tables or additional results.
• Data collection instruments.
• Ethical approval letters, confidentiality agreements.
Number: Appendix A, B… with descriptive titles.

generic.phd.description: Profile for master's and doctorate: literature review, state of the art, approach, experimentation, glossary and acronyms. XeLaTeX, biber, APA 7.

vancouver.health.name: Health Sciences (IMRaD)

title_page.guidance:
The cover page is automatically generated with the project data.
You don't need to write content here.

table_of_contents.guidance:
The index is generated automatically.
You don't need to write anything here.

abstract_es.title: Abstract
abstract_es.guidance:
The IMRaD abstract is structured with the same subtitles as the article, in miniature:
• Objective: a sentence with the purpose of the study.
• Material and methods: design, population, intervention and main measurements.
• Results: more relevant findings with numerical data.
• Conclusions: clinical interpretation and scope.
Limit: 250 words for thesis (varies by institution). No citations. No undefined acronyms.
At the end: 3–6 MeSH (Medical Subject Headings) Keywords.

abstract_en.title: Abstract
abstract_en.guidance:
Faithful translation of the abstract into English with the same subtitles: Objective, Methods, Results, Conclusions.
Keywords: MeSH terms in English.
Required for indexing in PubMed/MEDLINE and presentation at international conferences.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.guidance:
In IMRaD, the Introduction answers: what is known? what is not known? what is going to be studied?
Recommended structure (funnel):
1. Magnitude of the health problem (epidemiology, disease burden).
2. What is known: selective review of the literature with Vancouver citations ([1], [2]…).
3. Gap of knowledge or controversy that motivates the study.
4. Research question or objective of the study (clearly stated).
5. Hypotheses if applicable.
Do not present results here. Typical length: 2–4 pages.

materials_methods.title: Material and methods
materials_methods.guidance:
Describe the study in enough detail so that it can be replicated. Includes:
• Study design: experimental, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, systematic review, etc.
• Place and period of the study.
• Population: inclusion and exclusion criteria.
• Sample: size, sampling technique, statistical justification.
• Intervention (if applicable): exact description, dose, duration.
• Variables and measurement instruments.
• Statistical analysis: tests used, software, significance level.
• Ethical considerations: ethics committee approval, informed consent.
Avoid justifying methodological decisions — just describe them.

results.title: Results
results.guidance:
Present the findings objectively and without interpretation:
• Start with the characteristics of the sample (Table 1: baseline characteristics).
• Presents the results in the order of the objectives or hypotheses.
• Use tables and figures for numerical data — each referenced in the text.
• Reports: n, %, means ± SD, medians (IQR), RR, OR, 95% CI, p value.
• Do not repeat in text what the table already shows — comment only on what is most relevant.
• For qualitative studies: categories with textual quotes from participants (anonymous).

discussion.title: Discussion
discussion.guidance:
It is the most analytical section and the most difficult to write. You must:
• Return to the objective of the study and summarize the main finding.
• Compare your results with previous studies (similar, different and contradictory).
• Explain discrepancies: differences in design, population, context.
• Point out clinical implications: what changes in practice?
• Acknowledge the limitations of the study (don't minimize them — it reinforces credibility).
• Suggest specific future research.
Do not present new results here.

conclusions.title: Conclusions
conclusions.guidance:
In many biomedical articles the conclusions are included in the Discussion.
If your institution requires them separately:
• One or two sentences per objective answered.
• Directly answers the research question.
• Avoid generalizing beyond what the data allows.
• Mentions the contribution to knowledge or clinical practice.

references.title: References
references.guidance:
Vancouver style: numerical references in order of appearance in the text ([1], [2]…).
The list is automatically generated from your .bib when you compile.
Prioritizes sources indexed in MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science.
Use the DOI importer to add articles with one click — Crossref has the most PubMed.
Reference limit: varies by institution (common: 30–50 for theses).

appendices.title: Annexes
appendices.guidance:
Includes supporting documents that do not fit in the text:
• Collection instrument (questionnaire, data capture sheet).
• Letter of approval from the ethics committee.
• Informed consent.
• Raw or supplementary data tables.
• Detailed intervention protocol.
Number: Annex A, B… and refer to them from the text.

vancouver.health.description: IMRaD structure for clinical and biomedical research. Vancouver style bibliography. Ideal for medicine, nursing and health sciences theses.

apa.basic.name: Basic APA

title_page.guidance:
The APA 7 cover page is automatically generated with the project data.
Includes: title, author(s), institution, subject, teacher's name and date.
You don't need to write content here.

abstract_es.title: Abstract
abstract_es.guidance:
The APA 7 abstract goes on a separate page with the heading "Abstract" (centered, bold).
150–250 words that answer: what is studied?, how?, what was found?, what does it mean?
At the end include 4–6 Keywords: in italics.
Do not cite references in the abstract.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.guidance:
In APA 7, the introduction does not carry the heading "Introduction" — the profile handles it automatically.
You must present:
• The topic and its relevance.
• What is known so far (brief bibliographic synthesis).
• The purpose or objective of the work.
• The question or hypothesis does apply.
Use APA citations in text: (Last Name, Year) or Last Name (Year) depending on the flow.

development.title: Development
development.guidance:
Main body of the work. Organize with level 2 and 3 headings based on complexity.
For essays: main argument, supporting arguments with bibliographic evidence, counterarguments.
For reports: conceptual framework, analysis, findings.
Paraphrase sources — avoid long verbatim quotes (use them only when the exact words matter).
Cite everything that is not your own creation.

conclusions.title: Conclusions
conclusions.guidance:
Synthesize the main points of the work:
• Answers the question or purpose posed in the introduction.
• Point out implications of the findings.
• Recognize limitations.
• Suggests lines of future work or research.
Don't include new quotes here. Length: 1–2 pages.

references.title: References
references.guidance:
In APA 7 it is called "References" (not "Bibliography").
The list is automatically generated from your .bib when you compile.
APA 7 rules: arranged alphabetically, hanging indent, URL or DOI at the end of each entry.
Use the DOI importer (Ctrl+[ > DOI panel) to add references with one click.

apa.basic.description: Simplified profile for academic works with strict APA 7 style. Ideal for reports, essays and short articles.

chicago.humanities.name: Chicago / Turabian — Humanities

title_page.guidance:
The Turabian cover includes: title (centered, one-third from top), author's name, program and university, city and year. No page number.
The profile generates the cover page with the project data.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.guidance:
Turabian recommends an abstract of 150–350 words for doctoral dissertations.
Includes: theme, approach, main argument, methodology and conclusion.
Write it in present or past tense — choose one and be consistent.

table_of_contents.guidance: The index is generated automatically. In Chicago, chapter and section levels are included, but not subsections from level 3 onwards.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.guidance:
In humanities the introduction presents the central argument (thesis statement), the corpus or main sources, the methodology and the justification.
Chicago allows for a more discursive style than other disciplines — you can use the first person and develop the argument with nuances from the beginning.
Citations are in numbered footnotes, not in parentheses. The system inserts them automatically.

chapter_1.title: Chapter 1
chapter_1.guidance:
In humanities the chapters develop the argument progressively.
Each chapter must have its own argument that contributes to the central argument of the thesis.
Use footnotes for direct quotes, references, and extensive comments that would interrupt the flow of the text.
Short footnotes can be quotes; the long ones can be additional discussions.

chapter_2.title: Chapter 2
chapter_2.guidance:
Second chapter. Develop the next step of the argument.
In history or literature, this chapter may analyze a corpus of texts, historical period, or set of primary sources.
Cite primary and secondary sources with footnotes. For recurring primary sources, use abbreviations in a footnote after the first full citation.

chapter_3.title: Chapter 3
chapter_3.guidance:
Third chapter. It brings the argument to its point of greatest development.
You can add or remove chapters depending on the structure of your thesis — most humanities dissertations have 3–5 chapters.

conclusions.title: Conclusions
conclusions.guidance:
The conclusions take up the central argument and enrich it with what was learned in the chapters.
Avoid repeating what has already been said. It opens towards broader implications, open debates and possible future research.
In the humanities it is valid — and sometimes necessary — to conclude with nuances or open questions.

bibliography.title: Bibliography
bibliography.guidance:
In Chicago Notes-Bibliography the final list is called "Bibliography" (not "References").
It is arranged alphabetically by author's last name.
The bibliography is automatically generated from your .bib when you compile.
Include all cited sources in footnotes — and you can include sources consulted but not cited if they add context.

appendices.title: Appendices
appendices.guidance: In the humanities, appendices usually include: transcriptions of primary sources, complete interviews, additional visual material, chronologies or glossaries of specialized terms.

chicago.humanities.description: Theses and dissertations in humanities, social sciences and arts with style Chicago Notes-Bibliography (17th ed.) / Turabian 9th ed. Citations are in numbered footnotes, not in parentheses. Bibliography at the end arranged alphabetically. Widely used in philosophy, history, literature, social sciences and law.

mx.ipn.esfm.name: IPN ESFM — Physics and Mathematics

portada.guidance:
The ESFM cover includes: IPN shield, "Higher School of Physics and Mathematics", title of the work, type of work (Thesis to obtain the title/degree of...), name of the student, director(s), place and year.
The profile is generated with the project data.

resumen.title: Abstract
resumen.guidance:
Abstract of 150–250 words. In physics and mathematics it must be precise:
• The central problem or question, expressed without unnecessary jargon.
• The main approach or method.
• The most important result (with the measurement or dimension if applicable).
• The implication or application of the result.
Avoid equations in the abstract. Define the acronyms you do use.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.guidance: English translation of the abstract. Recommended if you plan to publish or present at international conferences.

tabla_contenidos.guidance: The index is generated automatically. In mathematical works it is common to also include a list of notations and symbols before the introduction.

introduccion.title: Introduction
introduccion.guidance:
The introduction in physics/mathematics places the work in the context of the discipline:
• Motivation: why is the problem interesting or relevant?
• Background: directly related previous work.
• Precise statement of the problem or research question.
• Main results (announces without demonstrating — that goes in the body).
• Document structure.
You can use mathematical notation from here, but keep it accessible.

preliminares.title: Preliminaries
preliminares.guidance:
Section where you define the mathematical language that you will use in the rest of the work.
Includes: fundamental definitions, notation, and known results that you will need to cite.
Do not demonstrate known results unless they are necessary to establish the exact notation.
Use the editor's Theorem, Definition, and Lemma blocks to structure your content.
Structure example: "Definition 2.1 (Hilbert Space)...", "Lemma 2.3...", "Theorem 2.5 (Spectral)..."

desarrollo.title: Development
desarrollo.guidance:
The main body of the work. In pure mathematics: the development of theory with complete proofs.
In physics: the development of the model, theory or experiment.
Structure each chapter with propositions, lemmas, theorems and proofs.
Each demo must explicitly close with □ or "∎" (the editor inserts this automatically).
Numbered equations should be referenced from the text: use \eqref{} or \cref{}.

resultados.title: Results and Applications
resultados.guidance:
If your work has numerical, computational or experimental applications, submit them here.
For computational physics: includes simulation parameters, convergence and comparison with analytical or experimental results.
For experimental physics: presents data with uncertainties, statistical analysis and graphs.

conclusiones.title: Conclusions
conclusiones.guidance:
Summarizes the results obtained and their relevance.
In mathematics: what conjectures were solved, what questions the work opens.
In physics: what phenomena were explained, what predictions the model makes.
Clearly indicate what is original in your work vs. what is known
Point out open problems or natural extensions of the work.

referencias.title: References
referencias.guidance:
List of references in APA 7 (automatically generated).
For articles from physics/mathematics journals use the DOI importer — Crossref has the most articles from Physical Review, Journal of Mathematical Physics, etc.
For classic textbooks (Rudin, Spivak, Peskin & Schroeder, etc.): add the entry manually to the .bib if they are not in Crossref.

apendices.title: Appendices
apendices.guidance: Supplementary technical material: long demonstrations that would interrupt the flow of the main argument, detailed calculations, simulation code, tables of experimental data.

mx.ipn.esfm.description: Undergraduate and postgraduate thesis from the Higher School of Physics and Mathematics of the IPN. Designed for works with high mathematical density: theorems, lemmas, corollaries, proofs, physical notation and complex equations. APA bibliography for general works, or numerical style for physics publications.

mx.ipn.sepi.name: IPN SEPI — Postgraduate in Engineering and Sciences

portada.guidance:
The IPN-SEPI cover includes: IPN shield, name of the academic unit (ESIME/ESCOM/UPIITA...), title of the work, type of thesis (to obtain the degree of Master/Doctor in...), name of the student, thesis directors, place and year.
The profile generates the cover page with the project data.

resumen.title: Abstract
resumen.guidance:
Technical abstract in Spanish of 200–300 words. The SEPI requires it in Spanish.
It must contain: objective, methodology, main results and conclusion.
In the end: 5–8 technical keywords.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.guidance:
English translation of the abstract. The SEPI-IPN requires it in all postgraduate programs.
Keywords: same as in Spanish, in English.

tabla_contenidos.guidance: The index is generated automatically. The IPN also requires a list of figures, a list of tables and, if applicable, a list of algorithms or code listings.

introduccion.title: Introduction
introduccion.guidance:
The IPN-SEPI introduction must include:
1. Technological or scientific context of the problem.
2. Motivation and justification.
3. Hypothesis or research question.
4. General objective and specific objectives.
5. Scope and limitations.
6. Organization of the document.
Citations in IEEE are numerical: [1], [2], [3]…

estado_arte.title: State of the Art
estado_arte.guidance:
Critical review of the state of the art. In the SEPI-IPN it is mandatory and must:
• Identify the most relevant works (last 5–10 years; IEEE/ACM/Elsevier conferences and journals).
• Compare approaches: comparative tables of methods, results and limitations.
• Identify the gap or limitation that your work solves.
• Justify why your proposal is different or superior.
Citation with number in brackets: "Pérez et al. [5] proposed..."

metodologia.title: Methodology or Development
metodologia.guidance:
In engineering the methodology describes the proposed solution:
• System architecture or design.
• Mathematical or formal model if applicable.
• Algorithms developed (use the Algorithm block).
• Implementation: languages, frameworks, hardware.
• General flow diagram of the system.
The level of detail must allow the work to be replicated.

resultados.title: Results and Analysis
resultados.guidance:
Present and analyze experimental or simulation results:
• Experimental setup: equipment, parameters, conditions.
• Evaluation metrics: precision, time, consumption, performance, etc.
• Comparison with the state of the art (comparative table).
• Statistical analysis if applicable (mean, deviation, confidence interval).
In IEEE each figure and table must have a number and concise description.

conclusiones.title: Conclusions and Future Work
conclusiones.guidance:
Close the work with technical rigor:
• Objectives achieved vs. raised.
• Original contributions of the work.
• Identified technical limitations.
• Future work: concrete improvements, possible extensions, open problems.
The IPN-SEPI especially values ​​the mention of possible publications or industrial applications.

referencias.title: References
referencias.guidance:
In IEEE the references are numerical in order of appearance.
The list is automatically generated from your .bib.
For IEEE and ACM articles: use the DOI importer.
The IPN requires including the DOI when available.

anexos.title: Annexes
anexos.guidance:
Complete source code, scripts, hardware/software configurations, datasheets, user manuals, raw experiment data.
Number: Annex A, Annex B… and reference each one from the text.

mx.ipn.sepi.description: Thesis of the Postgraduate Studies and Research Section (SEPI) of the National Polytechnic Institute. Applies to CINVESTAV, ESIME, ESCOM, UPIITA and SEPI units. IEEE Bibliography for Engineering and Technology; IPN format with margins, typography and structure specific to the Postgraduate and Research Directorate.

mx.ipn.upibi.name: IPN UPIBI — Biotechnology

portada.guidance: The UPIBI cover includes: IPN shield, "Interdisciplinary Professional Unit of Biotechnology", career or program, title of the work, type of thesis, name of the student, director(s), place and year.

resumen.title: Abstract
resumen.guidance:
Scientific abstract of 200–300 words in Spanish. In biotechnology the abstract must include:
• Objective of the study.
• Main materials/organisms/strains/samples used.
• Core methodology (type of experiment, key analytical technique).
• Most important result (with quantitative data if possible).
• Conclusion or application.
At the end: 5–8 keywords in Spanish.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.guidance:
English translation of the abstract. The UPIBI requires it for all degree and postgraduate work.
Keywords in English: same as in Spanish.

tabla_contenidos.guidance: Automatically generated index. In works with many figures (gels, chromatograms, growth curves), it includes a list of figures and a list of tables.

introduccion.title: Introduction
introduccion.guidance:
The introduction to biotechnology contextualizes the problem from biology and engineering:
• Importance of the microorganism, process, compound or problem studied.
• State of the art: relevant previous works (use APA: Author, year).
• Rationale: why is this study relevant?
• Working hypothesis (if the design is experimental).
• General objective and specific objectives.
Be specific on taxa, strains, conditions and compounds from the start.

marco_teorico.title: Theoretical Framework
marco_teorico.guidance:
Bases the work on scientific literature:
• Biology/biochemistry of the system studied (microorganism, enzyme, metabolic pathway, etc.).
• Principles of the main process or technique (fermentation, HPLC, PCR, etc.).
• Kinetic or mathematical models if applicable (Michaelis-Menten, Monod, etc.).
• Standards or regulations if relevant (NOM, FDA, WHO).

materiales_metodos.title: Materials and Methods
materiales_metodos.guidance:
In biotechnology the materials and methods section is critical for reproducibility. Includes:
• Biological materials: organisms, strains (with catalog number or accession number), cell lines, samples (with origin and conservation conditions).
• Reagents: name, grade, supplier.
• Equipment: model, brand, operating conditions.
• Analytical methods: exact conditions (temperature, pH, time, concentrations).
• Experimental design: independent, dependent and control variables; replicas.
• Statistical analysis: software, tests and significance level (α = 0.05).
The level of detail should allow another laboratory to repeat the experiment exactly.

resultados.title: Results
resultados.guidance:
Present the data objectively, without interpretation:
• Figures: chromatograms, growth curves, gels, microscopies — each with number, descriptive title (below), and complete units on the axes.
• Tables: tabulated data with mean ± standard deviation, units in the header.
• Statistics: indicates whether the differences are significant (p < 0.05, ANOVA, Tukey, etc.).
• Statistical letters in tables and figures if applicable (a, b, ab for homogeneous groups).
Refer to each figure or table explicitly in the text before it appears.

discusion.title: Discussion
discusion.guidance:
Interpret the results in the context of the literature:
• Do the results confirm or refute the hypothesis?
• Compare with previous studies: do they match? do they differ? Why might they differ (strain, conditions, method)?
• Explains biological or biochemical mechanisms that justify the results.
• Discusses methodological limitations and their impact on the results.
• Implications: what does it mean for industry, medicine or the environment?

conclusiones.title: Conclusions
conclusiones.guidance:
Summarize the most important things in direct and measurable terms:
• Each conclusion corresponds to a specific objective.
• Avoid repeating the abstract of results — it concludes, does not report.
• Indicates the contribution to knowledge or the industry.
• Recommendations for future research.

referencias.title: References
referencias.guidance:
List of references in APA 7 (automatically generated).
For scientific articles: use the DOI importer — PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science have DOIs for most biotechnology articles.
For articles without DOI: include the URL of the journal or database.

anexos.title: Annexes
anexos.guidance: Raw data from experiments, complete gels (untrimmed), nucleotide or amino acid sequences, GenBank accession numbers, certificates of reagent analysis, complete protocols not included in M&M.

mx.ipn.upibi.description: Thesis of the Interdisciplinary Professional Unit of Biotechnology of the IPN. It covers biochemistry, microbiology, bioprocess engineering, bioinformatics, environmental and pharmaceutical biotechnology. Experimental and quantitative nature with high rigor in data presentation. APA 7 bibliography for most areas; Vancouver accepted in areas closer to health sciences.

mx.ipn.upitta.name: IPN UPITTA — Advanced Technologies

portada.guidance: The UPITTA cover includes: IPN shield, "Interdisciplinary Professional Unit of Advanced Technologies", title of the work, type of thesis, name of the student, directors, place and year.

resumen.title: Abstract
resumen.guidance:
Technical abstract in Spanish of 200–250 words. The interdisciplinary nature of UPITTA means that the abstract must be understandable for readers from different areas (engineering, computing, applied mathematics).
Includes: technical problem, proposed solution, key technologies and main measurable result.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.guidance:
English translation. Required by UPITTA for all degree and postgraduate work.
Keywords in English: 5–8 relevant technical terms.

tabla_contenidos.guidance: Automatically generated index. Includes list of figures and list of tables if there are more than 5 of each type.

introduccion.title: Introduction
introduccion.guidance:
Contextualize the problem from the interdisciplinary perspective of UPITTA:
• The technological area and its relevance (mechatronics, AI, automation, etc.).
• The specific problem and its impact (industrial, social, scientific).
• Most important related works (citation with IEEE number: [1], [2]).
• General objective and specific objectives.
• Concrete contribution: what do you propose that does not exist or does not work well?
• Document organization.

estado_arte.title: State of the Art and Theoretical Framework
estado_arte.guidance:
Combination of the state of the art and the theoretical framework, appropriate for interdisciplinary work:
• Review the most relevant previous works in each area that your project touches.
• Present the theories or mathematical models on which your solution is based.
• Comparative tables of existing solutions vs. yours.
• Clearly identify the niche or improvement that your work brings.
At UPITTA the interdisciplinary approach is a strength — it shows how you integrate different areas.

diseno.title: System Design
diseno.guidance:
Present the complete architecture or design of the system before implementing it:
• General architecture: block or component diagram.
• Mathematical or dynamic model (for control systems, robotics, etc.).
• Selection and justification of technologies (sensors, actuators, platforms, algorithms).
• Flowcharts or state machines if applicable.
• Design constraints: power, size, cost, response time.
The design must be independent of the implementation.

implementacion.title: Implementation and Results
implementacion.guidance:
Describe the implementation and present the experimental results:
• Development environment: hardware, software, versions.
• Implementation by modules or subsystems.
• Integration testing: Does the entire system work as the design predicts?
• Quantitative results: metrics (accuracy, response time, consumption, RMS error, etc.).
• Comparison with the state of the art or with the baseline.
At UPITTA, tests in real or quasi-real conditions are valued.

conclusiones.title: Conclusions and Future Work
conclusiones.guidance:
Close the work with technical and interdisciplinary rigor:
• Objectives met vs. raised (with quantitative evidence).
• Original contributions (technical, methodological, or disciplinary integration).
• Limitations of the system or the study.
• Future work: improvements, extensions, possible industrial or research applications.
Mention whether the work led or may lead to publications or patents.

referencias.title: References
referencias.guidance:
IEEE numerical references in order of appearance (automatically generated).
Use the DOI importer for articles from IEEE Xplore, ACM DL, etc.
Include the DOI in each reference — it is an IEEE requirement.

anexos.title: Annexes
anexos.guidance: Complete source code, component datasheets, mechanical or electrical drawings, calibration procedures, user manuals, raw experiment data.

mx.ipn.upitta.description: Thesis of the Interdisciplinary Professional Unit of Advanced Technologies of the IPN. Oriented to mechatronics, intelligent systems, automation, robotics and emerging technologies. Interdisciplinary nature: integrates engineering, computing and basic sciences. IEEE Numerical Bibliography.

mx.unam.posgrado.name: UNAM — Postgraduate

portada.guidance:
The UNAM cover includes: UNAM shield, name of the faculty or institute, title of the work, type of thesis (to obtain the Master's/Doctorate degree in...), name of the student, thesis director, tutorial committee, place and year.
The profile generates the cover automatically with the data you configured when creating the project.

dedicatoria.title: Dedication
dedicatoria.guidance:
Short text (1–5 lines) dedicated to important people. It is personal and optional.
At UNAM it does not have a page number and is printed on a separate page.

agradecimientos.title: Thanks
agradecimientos.guidance:
Mention the director, tutorial committee, CONACYT/CONAHCyT (if there was a scholarship), laboratory or research group, and key people in the work.
Include the project or scholarship number if applicable (e.g. "CONAHCyT Scholarship No. XXXXXX").

resumen.title: Abstract
resumen.guidance:
Abstract in Spanish of 200–300 words. The CEP-UNAM requires it in Spanish.
Includes: objective, methodology, main results and conclusion.
At the end: 4–6 keywords separated by semicolons.

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.guidance:
Translation of the abstract into English. Many UNAM doctoral programs require it.
Identical format to the abstract in Spanish.
Keywords: same as in Spanish, in English.

tabla_contenidos.guidance:
The index is generated automatically. Includes chapters, sections and subsections.
UNAM generally also requires a list of figures and a list of tables if there are more than 5.

introduccion.title: Introduction
introduccion.guidance:
The UNAM introduction must include:
1. Background and context of the problem.
2. Problem statement and justification.
3. Hypothesis or research question.
4. General objective and specific objectives.
5. Scope and limitations.
6. Structure of the thesis (what each chapter contains).
Recommended length: 4–8 pages.

marco_teorico.title: Theoretical Framework
marco_teorico.guidance:
Review and synthesize relevant literature. At UNAM the theoretical framework must:
• Cite primary and current sources (last 10 years; classics if they are fundamental).
• Organize ideas logically, not as a list of summaries.
• Use APA 7 for all citations — the system generates them automatically.
• Identify the state of the art and the gap that your research fills.

metodologia.title: Methodology
metodologia.guidance:
Describe the methodology in enough detail to be replicated. Includes:
• Type of research and design.
• Population, sample and selection criteria.
• Instruments and procedures.
• Data analysis (software, statistics or qualitative categories).
• Ethical considerations and consents if applicable.

resultados.title: Results
resultados.guidance:
Present the findings objectively. Use tables and figures with references in the text.
At UNAM each figure and table must have: number, descriptive title (above for tables, below for figures) and source if applicable.
Don't interpret the results here — that goes in the Discussion.

discusion.title: Discussion
discusion.guidance:
Interpret the results in the context of your research question and the literature.
Compare with previous studies, point out coincidences and divergences.
Discusses theoretical and practical implications.
Recognize limitations honestly.

conclusiones.title: Conclusions
conclusiones.guidance:
Respond directly to your objectives and hypotheses. The CEP-UNAM hopes:
• Synthesis of main findings.
• Original contributions to the field.
• Recommendations for future research.
• Implications for practice or policy (if applicable).
Length: 3–5 pages. Do not enter new information.

referencias.title: References
referencias.guidance:
The reference list is automatically generated in APA 7 format.
UNAM requires APA 7 in most graduate programs.
Make sure each source cited is in the .bib, and vice versa.
Use the DOI importer to get complete and normalized entries.

anexos.title: Annexes
anexos.guidance:
Supplementary material that supports the work without interrupting the main flow:
collection instruments, raw data tables, source code, consent letters.
Number: Annex A, Annex B… Reference each one from the main text.

mx.unam.posgrado.description: Postgraduate theses and dissertations from the National Autonomous University of Mexico. Based on the guidelines of the Coordination of Postgraduate Studies (CEP-UNAM): letter or legal size paper, 2.5 cm margins, 1.5 line spacing, APA 7, cover with official coat of arms.

generic.tesina.name: Generic dissertation

title_page.guidance:
The cover page is automatically generated with the institutional data configured when creating the project.
You don't need to write content here.

table_of_contents.guidance:
The index is automatically generated from your enabled sections.
You don't need to write anything here.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.guidance:
The introduction presents the topic and motivates the work. For a thesis it includes:
1. Brief context of the topic (from general to specific).
2. Problem or question that the work addresses.
3. General objective.
4. Justification: why is it relevant to study it?
5. Brief description of how the document is organized.
Typical length: 1–3 pages.

development.title: Development
development.guidance:
Development is the central body of the work. Break it down into logical subsections:
• Conceptual framework: defines key concepts with bibliographic support.
• Analysis or development of the topic: argument, proposal or central study.
• Results or findings if applicable.
Each idea must be supported by sources. Use "Bibliographical citation" blocks for referencing.
Typical length: 10–30 pages.

conclusions.title: Conclusions
conclusions.guidance:
Close the work by directly responding to the objective stated in the introduction:
• Was the objective achieved? What was found?
• Reflection on the relevance of the work.
• Limitations found.
• Recommendations or lines of future work.
Typical length: 1–2 pages. Do not enter new information here.

references.guidance:
The reference list is automatically generated from your .bib file when you compile.
Use the DOI importer (Ctrl+[ > DOI panel) to easily add sources.
APA 7 style is applied automatically.

generic.tesina.description: Simplified version for bachelor's degree: introduction, development and conclusions. Book class, XeLaTeX, biber, APA 7.

generic.thesis.name: Generic thesis

title_page.guidance:
The cover page is automatically generated by the profile with the institutional data that you configured when creating the project (student name, institution, job title, thesis director, year).
You don't need to write content here.

table_of_contents.guidance:
The table of contents is automatically generated from the sections enabled in your project.
You don't need to write anything — just make sure your chapters have titles.

abstract_es.title: Summary
abstract_es.guidance:
The abstract presents your thesis in 150–250 words. You must answer briefly:
• What is the problem or research question?
• What methodology did you use?
• What are the main results?
• What is the conclusion or contribution?
Do not cite references in the summary. Write it in the past tense. Include 4–6 keywords at the end.

abstract_en.title: Abstract
abstract_en.guidance:
Faithful translation of the summary into English, in the same format (150–250 words).
Many graduate institutions require it for international indexing.
Keywords: same keywords as the summary, in English.

dedication.title: Dedication
dedication.guidance:
Short text (1–5 lines) dedicated to people important to the author.
It is personal and optional. Some examples: "To my parents, for their unconditional support."
It does not have an explicit title in most styles — the profile handles it.

acknowledgements.title: Thanks
acknowledgements.guidance:
Mention those who contributed to your research: director, readers, colleagues, institutions, funders.
Be specific: mention the role of each person or organization.
Recommended length: half to one page.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.guidance:
The introduction contextualizes your work and motivates the reader to continue reading. Must include:
1. General context of the topic (from broad to specific).
2. Problem statement: what gap or need exists?
3. Research question or hypothesis.
4. General objective and specific objectives.
5. Rationale: why is it relevant to study this?
6. Scope and limitations of the study.
7. Brief description of the structure of the thesis.
Typical length: 3–6 pages.

theoretical_framework.title: Theoretical Framework
theoretical_framework.guidance:
The theoretical framework supports your research with existing literature. You must:
• Review key concepts and theories related to your topic.
• Cite primary and current sources (last 5–10 years for articles; classics if they are fundamental).
• Organize ideas logically, not as a list of summaries.
• Identify the state of the art: what is known and what is missing?
• Position your work within literature: what do you contribute?
Use the "Bibliographic citation" block for each reference. Avoid excessive quotes — paraphrase and analyze.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.guidance:
Describe how you conducted your research in enough detail so that it can be replicated. Includes:
• Type of research (quantitative, qualitative, mixed; exploratory, descriptive, explanatory).
• Design: experimental, quasi-experimental, case study, survey, etc.
• Population and sample: selection criteria, size, sampling technique.
• Collection instruments: questionnaires, interviews, observation, experiments.
• Procedure: steps followed chronologically.
• Data analysis: software, statistics, qualitative analysis categories.
• Ethical considerations if applicable.

results.title: Results
results.guidance:
Present the findings of your research objectively, without yet interpreting them. Guides:
• Organize the results following the order of your objectives or research questions.
• Use tables and figures for numerical or comparative data — reference each in the text.
• Do not repeat in text what a table already shows; Comment the most relevant.
• Be precise with figures: include units, percentages, statistical values ​​(p, r, χ², etc.).
• For qualitative research: presents categories with illustrative textual quotes.

discussion.title: Discussion
discussion.guidance:
Here you interpret your results and relate them to the literature. It is the most analytical section. You must:
• Explain what your results mean in the context of your research question.
• Compare with previous studies: do they match? do they differ? because?
• Point out unexpected results and offer possible explanations.
• Discuss theoretical and practical implications of your findings.
• Recognize the limitations of the study honestly.
Do not present new results here — only interpret those already reported.

conclusions.title: Conclusions
conclusions.guidance:
Conclusions close your argument and respond directly to your objectives. Includes:
• Answer to the research question / hypothesis verification.
• Synthesis of the most important findings (without repeating details of results).
• Original contributions of the work.
• Recommendations for professional practice or future research.
• Final reflection on the relevance of the work.
Recommended length: 2–4 pages. Do not enter new information.

references.title: References
references.guidance:
The reference list is automatically generated from your .bib file when you compile.
Make sure every source cited in the text is in the .bib, and vice versa.
To add references: use the import DOI button or edit the references.bib file directly.
The citation style (APA 7 in this profile) is applied automatically by LaTeX.

appendices.title: Annexes
appendices.guidance:
The annexes contain supporting material that does not fit in the main body but that the reader may need to verify:
• Collection instruments (complete questionnaires, interview guides).
• Raw data tables.
• Source code or scripts.
• Maps, plans, legal documents.
• Letters of authorization or informed consent.
Each annex must be numbered (Annex A, Annex B...) and referenced from the main text.

generic.thesis.description: Base profile for theses and formal academic works for bachelor's, specialty, master's, doctoral and postdoctoral degrees. Book class, XeLaTeX, biber, APA 7.

chicago17_notes.name: Chicago 17 (Notes)
chicago17_notes.description: Notes-Bibliography system used in humanities disciplines. Citations appear as footnotes or endnotes; a full bibliography is included at the end. Preferred at Harvard, UChicago, and many UK and US humanities departments.

gb7714.name: GB/T 7714
gb7714.description: Mandatory Chinese national standard for bibliographic references in academic works. Numeric style, ordered by appearance. Required at Tsinghua, Peking University, Fudan, Zhejiang, and all Chinese universities for Chinese-language theses.

harvard.name: Harvard
harvard.description: Author-date style similar to APA, widely used in UK and Australian universities. Common in business, management, and social science programs outside the USA. No single authoritative manual — institutions often define their own variant.

mhra.name: MHRA
mhra.description: UK humanities standard similar to Chicago Notes-Bibliography. Widely required at Oxford, Cambridge, UCL, and other Russell Group universities for dissertations in history, literature, and arts.

mla9.name: MLA 9
mla9.description: Standard for language, literature, and cultural studies in North America. Uses parenthetical author-page citations. Ninth edition (2021) simplified formatting rules and introduced more flexible source types.
